Set how long the app waits before reacting to place changes. Longer delays improve accuracy but may slow notifications, especially if the system limits the app.
Choose how the app obtains a more accurate location during the selected delay. This helps improve alert accuracy with slightly increased battery usage.
Place movements are processed immediately. May produce more false place alerts if your signal is weak or you drive past the place.
Depending on current location accuracy, app can wait anywhere between 0-10 seconds before reacting to place movements.
Depending on current location accuracy, app can wait up to 5–15 seconds before reacting to place movements. Some alerts might fail if the system stops the app while processing.
Waits up to 20-30 seconds before reacting to place movements. This will delay notifications, so make sure you are connected to the Internet and the app can run in the background without restrictions.
Place alert will be ignored if the app can not confirm the location as accurate. This might cause legitimate place movements to be ignored or delayed.
Place alert will be processed as usual. Uses less battery but might produce false positives.
Refresh Only if Location Is Inaccurate
Skips refresh if the current location is already accurate. Saves battery, but a wrong system location might cause false events.
The app will always try to get an accurate location. Might use more battery but improves alert accuracy.
Saves battery and trusts system accuracy. May cause false alerts with weak signal.
Gets an accurate location beforehand but may suppress or delay some alerts. Make sure you are connected to the Internet and the app can run in the background without restrictions.
An accurate location is requested as the final step to ensure you don’t miss any alerts, but it might cause extra or false alerts.
